summary: On Monday the 12th of Rabi al-Awwal, 11 AH, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away in the arms of his wife Aisha ؓ in Madinah. He was 63 years old. The news shook the companions profoundly; Umar ibn al-Khattab ؓ initially refused to believe it until Abu Bakr al-Siddiq ؓ recited the verse of Surah Al Imran that has anchored Muslim faith ever since.
narrative: Aisha ؓ narrates that on the morning of his passing, the Prophet ﷺ was resting with his head against her chest. She reports feeling him growing heavier as he leaned into her. He had a miswak (tooth-cleaning stick) and her young brother Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr came in with one; the Prophet ﷺ looked at it and she understood he wanted it. She softened it with her own teeth and offered it to him, and he cleaned his teeth with it. Then she reports: 'He ﷺ lay back in my lap, and I noticed his gaze fixed upward. His lips moved, and I leaned in. He said:

and then his hand went limp.' The phrase 'al-rafiq al-ala' — the highest companion — is understood as his choice of the next world over remaining in this one, the choice Allah had offered him.

This account is preserved in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim with multiple chains. The time of his passing is recorded in the classical sources as the forenoon (duha) of Monday, the 12th of Rabi al-Awwal, 11 AH. He was 63 years old — 63 lunar years. He had been with his community in Madinah for ten years and three months following the Hijrah.

When word spread from Aisha's ؓ house, Madinah was overtaken by grief. Ibn Hisham records that Umar ibn al-Khattab ؓ stood before the people with his sword drawn and declared that the Prophet ﷺ had not died but had gone to meet his Lord as Musa had gone, and would return to punish those who said he had died. He was in a state of profound shock.

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq ؓ arrived from his home at Sunh, entered Aisha's ؓ room, uncovered the Prophet's ﷺ face, kissed his forehead, and said: 'You are pure in life and in death.' He then came out and addressed the people: 'O people, whoever worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad is dead. And whoever worships Allah, then Allah is living and does not die.' He then recited the verse from Surah Al Imran (3:144): 'Muhammad is not but a Messenger. Messengers have passed before him. So if he were to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all. But Allah will reward the grateful.' Ibn Hisham records that it was as though this verse had never been recited before — everyone who heard Abu Bakr recite it that day understood it for the first time.

The Prophet ﷺ was washed by Ali ibn Abi Talib ؓ, al-Fadl ibn Abbas, Qutham ibn Abbas, and Usama ibn Zayd ؓ. He was shrouded in three white Yemeni cloths, with no shirt or turban. The companions prayed over him in groups without a single imam leading — standing over him individually and in small groups throughout the day and night. Al-Tabari and Ibn Hisham describe the procession of companions entering Aisha's room in waves to pray over him.

He was buried in the very room where he died — Aisha's ؓ chamber — based on a hadith that prophets are buried where they die. Ali ibn Abi Talib ؓ led the burial. Al-Tabari records that the grave was dug by Abu Talha al-Ansari and that it was a lahd (lateral niche) grave rather than a shaqq (straight trench). He was laid to rest at the spot where he had breathed his last, and the room remained inhabited by Aisha ؓ for many years. It was later incorporated into the expanded Masjid al-Nabawi, and the green dome that now marks the site is one of the most visited places on earth.

The Prophet ﷺ left no material wealth: his armour was pledged to a Jewish man of Madinah for a debt of thirty sa' of barley, his shield was not redeemed until after his death by Abu Bakr ؓ. His houses, land, and properties he had declared as sadaqah for the Muslim community. His true inheritance was the Quran and the Sunnah.
